Separatrices of the Lande-equation flow

Source: R/lande.R
lande_separatrices.Rd

Treats evolution of the mean phenotype as the flow \(\dot{\bar z} = G(\bar z) \nabla W(\bar z)\), with the G-matrix taken proportional to the local M-matrix of the genotype-phenotype map, and traces the separatrices between the basins of attraction of different optima: the stable manifolds of the saddle points of the landscape. Because G is positive definite, critical points and their types are those of the landscape; only the separatrices move. Two dimensions only.

Usage

lande_separatrices(
  model,
  landscape,
  lower = 0,
  upper = 12,
  step = 0.01,
  G = NULL,
  seed_step = 0.5,
  ds = 0.01,
  max_steps = 4000
)

Arguments

model

A `grn` model with two traits (used for the default `G`).

landscape

A 2D landscape function.

lower, upper

Bounds of the region (scalar or per dimension).

step

Grid spacing for the landscape derivatives.

G

Function of a phenotype returning the 2x2 G-matrix. Defaults to the model's M-matrix at that phenotype.

seed_step

Spacing of the starting points used to find critical points.

ds, max_steps

Arc-length step and maximum number of steps when tracing.

Value

Data frame of separatrix paths with columns `x1`, `x2`, `saddle`, `branch` and `step`. The saddle points are in `attr(, "saddles")`.

Details

The landscape is evaluated once on a grid; gradient and Hessian come from finite differences on that grid and are interpolated bilinearly (as in the original analysis scripts). Only the direction of the flow matters, so G can be given up to a scalar factor, and \(\nabla \ln W\) and \(\nabla W\) give the same separatrices.
